articles.title: Oregon hosting pair of 2028 top recruits for season opener
articles.summary: Oregon will host the nation's No. 2 recruit in the 2028 class, and the top in-state recruit for the season opener against Boise State.
articles.body:
The Oregon Ducks are wasting no time getting involved in the race for the top recruits in the 2028 recruiting class. Visits are already being lined up throughout the season, and the Ducks will have plenty of future talent on the sidelines for the season opener next weekend.

The Ducks locked in two more important visits for the first game of the season. Defensive lineman Kellan Hall, the No. 2 recruit in the 2028 class, and tight end Presley DeLance, the top recruit from Oregon, will both be in attendance at Autzen Stadium on Sept. 5.

Hall has already made a trip to Eugene this offseason and will be back to experience a game atmosphere against a tough opponent. The 6-foot-5, 275-pound pass rusher from Louisville, Kentucky, is a priority target for the Ducks, especially after the program missed on several defensive line targets in the 2027 class. Hall still has room to grow, and he could get bigger and stronger as a force on the interior.

Oklahoma is currently viewed as the favorite and will receive one of his 10 scheduled visits in the fall. However, Oregon has quickly built a rapport with Hall and is a key contender, alongside Kentucky, Georgia, Ohio State, Michigan, Notre Dame and more. There is still a long way to go in this recruiting process, but his athleticism as a big lineman makes him a highly coveted prospect.

The Ducks did a great job of keeping some of Oregon's top talents in-state in the 2027 cycle , landing commitments from the state's top four recruits. That effort isn't slowing down in the 2028 class, with DeLance, the top recruit in Oregon, taking a visit to Eugene.

The 6-foot-4 tight end from Lake Oswego is the No. 4 player at his position in the class, per 247Sports, after putting together a big spring and summer at different camps and landing several offers. He's quick for his size and can outrun defenders. He had a limited role as a sophomore, making just nine catches for 235 yards and a touchdown, but he is expected to see his role expand as a junior.

DeLance has scheduled eight visits for the fall and will begin his tour in the Pacific Northwest, visiting Oregon on Sept. 5 before making the trip north to visit Washington the next day. DeLance's teammate, edge rusher Josh Christensen , committed to the Ducks earlier in the offseason as part of the 2027 class, so the Ducks do have some support in the locker room.

Hall and DeLance are big targets for the Ducks, but they won't be alone on the sideline for the first game of the season. Multiple 2027 commits will be in attendance, as well as 2028 targets Jayden Bell and Tytan McNeal . It will be critical for the Ducks not only to start the season right with a victory, but to impress the next class of talent as well.

articles.title: John Cena reveals he and The Rock ‘really hated each other’ before WrestleMania showdown: Inside the bitter WWE rivalry where real-life resentment nearly sparked a backstage fight
articles.summary: WWE News: John Cena and The Rock are now viewed as WWE legends who share plenty of mutual respect. But before that relationship developed, the road to their Wre.
articles.body: John Cena and The Rock are now viewed as WWE legends who share plenty of mutual respect. But before that relationship developed, the road to their WrestleMania 28 showdown was filled with genuine tension, with Cena admitting that the hostility between them was not entirely part of the script.For more than a year, the two traded personal shots before finally meeting in the main event in Miami. Fans understood they were watching a manufactured rivalry play out. Cena later revealed the bad blood underneath it was real enough to worry him.Cena admits the hatred was realCena has explained that the promos sometimes tipped over from sports entertainment into something more personal."During a lot of moments leading up to that fight, we crossed the line of sports entertainment, and people could tell that we really hated each other," Cena said.The two men, by his own account, held genuinely different opinions of one another at the time. "Even though he had always been cordial to me, I did something foolish and started drumming up rumours about things I had no idea about," Cena added.None of this was standard promotional trash talk. Cena had publicly questioned The Rock's commitment to WWE after the former champion left to build a career in Hollywood.Why Cena had a problem with The RockThe Rock had walked away from the ring and become one of the biggest names in film. Cena, meanwhile, had settled into the role of WWE's leading full-time babyface, the guy who never left.He was particularly critical of The Rock pursuing acting while still talking up his love for wrestling. In 2010, Cena said: "He's genuinely nice guy. I've met him, and he's a fantastic human being."Then came the sting. He questioned why The Rock couldn't return for major occasions: "Just, don't f*** me around and tell me that you love [wrestling] when you're just doing it to do something else." Those comments became the fuel for everything that followed.Nearly coming to blowsWhen The Rock came back in 2011, it was first as host of WrestleMania 27. That involvement quickly hardened into a rivalry with Cena, setting up their meeting a year later.Things escalated through their promo battles on Raw. At one point Cena mocked The Rock for apparently using notes on his arm to remember lines, a jab that visibly angered him, and the confrontation reportedly turned heated backstage.Both men have since admitted how close it came to boiling over. "We might fail miserably at it," The Rock said of the risky approach they took to the rivalry. "But in this case it worked out very well and through all that edge and attitude and bite that we had and nearly coming to blows backstage and one night in the ring." He remembers the face-off getting genuinely intense: "Literally, we were nose-to-nose, it was any second."Cena knew The Rock would winFor a year, Cena publicly insisted there was no way The Rock would beat him. Privately, he'd known the outcome almost from the start."For a year straight I kept telling people that there is no way he was going to beat me, but I knew that he was going to win the moment the feud started," Cena said.However, reports at the time suggested WWE had initially considered having Cena win at WrestleMania 28 before changing course around the event. The final decision saw The Rock emerge victorious in his home state of Florida. Former referee Mike Chioda later recalled some backstage tension around the decision, with Cena having carried WWE as its full-time star for years before being asked to lose to a returning Rock.Cena apologised after losingOnce The Rock had pinned him, Cena did something that reshaped their relationship going forward. "The first thing I did after he beat me was apologise to his mother," he revealed. Then he walked straight into The Rock's locker room. "Then I went right into Dwayne's locker room and apologised to him."It didn't end the feud outright. The Rock beat CM Punk for the title at the following year's Royal Rumble, setting up a rematch at WrestleMania 29. This time Cena won.From genuine enemies to friendsThe rematch closed the book on the rivalry. Somewhere in the years after, genuine respect crept in, and eventually something like friendship, an odd outcome given how personal things had briefly become.There's an irony worth sitting with too. Cena spent years criticising The Rock for chasing Hollywood over wrestling. He later walked almost the same path himself, building a film career while trimming back his WWE schedule.None of this made Cena versus Rock memorable purely because of the size of the matches. It was that, for a stretch, nobody quite knew where the storyline ended and the real animosity began.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bournemouth 1-1 Everton: Match Report & Instant Reaction | Last gasp Tarkowski goal earns draw
articles.summary: Everton spurned a hatful of chances in the first half to go behind at Bournemouth, but captain Tarkowski equalized in time added on
articles.body:
AFC Bournemouth hosted Everton in a match that had historically favored the home side. Prior to this meeting, Bournemouth had proven to be a persistent bogey team for the Toffees, having won 9 of their 18 Premier League matchups. Everton had secured just one victory in their previous nine Premier League away games but that lone victory had come last season when the Toffees snuck a 1-0 win in December. Conversely, Bournemouth had enjoyed their own success against Everton later in the season, pulling off a disappointing 2-1 comeback victory at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium in February.

Coming into the match, Marco Rose's Bournemouth side had suffered a heartbreaking, late 2-1 defeat against Manchester City, where a Marcus Tavernier opener was cancelled out by two goals in the final six minutes. Meanwhile, after a clinical victory over Palace and then crushing Preston North End 4-0 behind a spectacular Thierno Barry hat-trick, Everton travelled to the south coast full of confidence.

The primary surprises in the lineup centered around Everton's midfield layout, where Harrison Armstrong unexpectedly started despite widespread reports in the morning suggesting he would miss the match due to advanced transfer talks with Nottingham Forest. Also, midfielder Hayden Hackney was a surprise omission from the opening eleven; having carried a minor injury knock with Moyes opting to protect him by placing him on the substitutes' bench and giving Garner another start.

The match began under cloudy skies with Everton controlling early possession and creating several dangerous opportunities. Everton were in their snazzy white away shirts with the Evertonians singing, "Don't sell Armstrong" from the kickoff.

Their best chances fell to Jarrad Branthwaite, whose glancing header was pawed away by Djordje Petrovic, and Thierno Barry, who missed a golden opportunity by firing a close-range rebound directly at the Bournemouth goalkeeper.

As the half progressed, the game grew increasingly chippy and end-to-end, testing both defenses. Jordan Pickford was forced into several sharp saves to deny dangerous breaks from Rayan and Justin Kluivert, while Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Adam Smith both picked up yellow cards for halting Everton attacks. Everton struggled with turnovers during this frantic period, allowing Bournemouth to grow into the game via sharp counterattacks.

The deadlock was finally broken just before the break when Bournemouth launched a quick counter. Evanilson held up the ball cleanly before feeding Alex Scott, who accurately picked out the far corner past a diving Pickford. As the players headed into the tunnel under a sudden torrential downpour, Everton manager David Moyes was left to ponder his tactical adjustments after a late response from Barry hit the side netting.

The second half commenced with no changes as Bournemouth kicked off, though Everton quickly pushed forward and created early attacking opportunities. Discipline became a factor as multiple players received yellow cards, and Everton had a penalty appeal turned down by VAR.

Both managers utilized their substitutes to alter the momentum of the game during the later stages. Bournemouth applied heavy pressure in the final twenty minutes, but Everton relied on desperate defending from Tarkowski and Mykolenko who made crucial blocks to stay in the match.

Everton pushed for a late breakthrough during the four minutes of added time, capitalizing on a corner kick. James Tarkowski reacted quickest to a loose ball in the box and slammed it into the far corner to secure a dramatic equalizer before the final whistle.

James Tarkowski – After struggling to cover Evanilson on the Bournemouth goal, the captain stepped up and did the job defensively to keep the match at one goal. The goal was reminiscent of his Merseyside Derby equalizer at Goodison as he drilled the ball low past Petrovic.

After the highs of Palace and Preston, the challenge of an away game against Bournemouth was a daunting one. Everton gave away the ball too frequently and struggled to deal with the Cherries counter attack. After going behind, the Blues continued to create chances and defend resolutely. Petrovic kept Everton at bay with some excellent saves and our defending kept us in the game so that the goal by Tarkowski in extra time was a fair result. The Blues also ended their streak of losing their first away game of the season at four years.

Everton applied 102 high intensity pressures in the final third against Crystal Palace last week, with only Leeds United and Manchester City making more across the first week of Premier League action. Also, no side had more shots (5) following a high turnover in the first week than the Toffees. This high intensity opening to the season was not on show today as Garner and Armstrong struggled in the middle of the park against a well organised Cherries team.

The morning news brought a shock report that claimed that Harrison Armstrong was the object of interest from Nottingham Forest. The Everton online pages were blowing up as everyone waited for the team list to be released. Thankfully, Armstrong started the match and there was a sense of relief. We have had a week of talk surrounding Ndiaye and this new report was more shocking. If TFG are considering this sale, you have to wonder what is going on at the club. Are we building or are we dismantling? The sooner this window closes the better. We have a good core to our team. Let us not throw that away.

Pickford – An alert save at the near post was impressive. Was hung out to dry on the goal. He commanded his area throughout the match.

Mykolenko – Allowed Scott too much room on the goal. A good block on the Kluivert shot prevented a goal.

Branthwaite – Solid in the middle but could have stepped up on the Scott goal.

Tarkowski – Very slow on Scott's goal but made a couple of goal saving blocks in the second half. His finish on the tying goal was quality.

Rohl – Some good tracking back to prevent a chance for Truffert. Lost possession a couple of times in dangerous places but showed tenacity to recover.

Armstrong – Struggled to get on the ball. Hopefully, he will be here next week to shine.

Garner – Looked well off the pace in the early going. Didn't track back well enough on the first Bournemouth goal.

George – His close ball control was off the charts but he faded as the game went on.

Dewsbury-Hall – Did lots of running and was the driving force going forward in the first half but lost the edge in the second half.

Ndiaye – Constantly draws players to him and his control is incredible.

Barry – Very isolated up front and should have done better when George's shot came back off the keeper.

articles.title: Carrick Rangers cruise to emphatic win over Bangor
articles.summary: Carrick Rangers cruise to a comprehensive 4-0 win over Bangor to make it three wins out of four to start the season.
articles.body:
Carrick Rangers produced a ruthless second-half display on their way to an emphatic 4-0 victory over Bangor at Clandeboye Park.

Matthew Snoddy broke the deadlock with an early strike before both Luke McCullough and Jimmy Callacher were denied by the woodwork.

Despite second-half pressure from the hosts, quickfire goals from Danny Gibson and Paul Heatley put the contest beyond reach before Joe Crowe sealed the rout with an 87th-minute stunner.

The result sees the visitors secure a third win in four league outings, while winless Bangor will be hoping to bounce back when they face the Welders in the County Antrim Shield.

The visitors got off to a dream start on seven minutes when Snoddy connected with Benjamin Buchanan-Rolleston's left-wing delivery, flicking the ball home at the front post.

That set the tone, and Stephen Baxter's side went close to doubling their advantage moments later when McCullough met Heatley's inswinging corner, only for the defender's left-footed effort from close range to cannon off the crossbar.

The chances kept coming for the away side, and on the stroke of half-time Carrick were unfortunate not to extend their lead when Callacher climbed highest to direct Heatley's curling set-piece against the woodwork.

Early in the second half, the Gers should have had their second when Mikey Place picked out Gibson with an inch-perfect cross, unmarked at the back post, and with goalkeeper Gareth Deane stranded, the striker somehow skied his effort over from point-blank range.

Gibson put that earlier miss to bed in style in the 70th minute, ghosting in behind the Bangor defence before slotting past a helpless Deane.

Heatley made sure of the points three minutes later, turning in from close range after a neat one-two with Gibson for his third league goal of the season.

A few minutes before the end, substitute Crowe added a fourth in sensational fashion, the midfielder tracking a flighted ball dropping over his shoulder before catching it sweetly on the full and rifling a blistering first-time volley past Deane.

Bangor manager Lee Feeney: "We were lucky it was only four. It was a tough one to take; I thought we were very, very naive in everything we've done. Just reflecting on it now, it could have been more, but we have to think about things and see how to approach games moving forward."

"We know what they're all about; they're the best in the league at what they do. For me, it was too easy a cross to come in and run into the blind side of our defenders, so it's everything we spoke about in the team talk not to let happen. We regrouped well and had plenty of the ball, but they just kept picking us off when we lost it."

"There was a lack of discipline and lack of experience at the back, there was no organisation, and we were leaving ourselves open, and it was just really, really disappointing."

Carrick Rangers boss Stephen Baxter: "Scoring four goals away from home without reply is always good, and we hit the woodwork numerous times as well, so that probably says a little bit about our dominance in the final third whenever we were attacking."

"Bangor had their moments and were very good in the first 20 minutes of the second half, but once we scored the second goal we started to take the game away from them."

"Paul Heatley and Danny Gibson are a lethal force when they get going, and our back three of Luke McCullough, Jimmy Callacher and BJ Burns gave us a masterclass in how to pass, play and hold a shape."

articles.title: New York Yankees vs. Boston Red Sox: Carlos Rodón vs. Jake Bennett
articles.summary: The Yankees play two today. Let’s start it with a bang?
articles.body:
A 1-0 win is as nailbiting as it gets, but it's still a win. The Yankees took the first round of this big four-game series last night, setting them up well for a good weekend. Hopefully they can do it in a less-stressful way, with two games against the Red Sox today and sending lefties to the hill in both of them.

Carlos Rodón does get the ball for the day half of today's doubleheader, signaling a grumpy day for me. He's on a three-win pace if he had been healthy all year, which is more than enough given he's the fourth option in the rotation, but the aesthetic experience of him is far worse than the analytical. He's only gone four innings his last two starts, despite allowing a single earned run in both, because his control has been rather spotty since coming off the IL (and he's had a pitch count to consider). On a day where we'll play two, let's hope he figures out a bit of length and saves a bullpen that may be needed with Max Fried coming off the injured list himself. Rodón threw 76 pitches in his last outing, so that's the baseline.

Before opening FanGraphs, I could have sworn Jake Bennett was an MLB: The Show create-a-player, but the 6-foot-6 lefty does seem to be a real person. Boston seems to run this pattern of large lefties who don't strike many people out but somehow never give up home runs, and Bennett follows this archetype. I regret to inform Yankee fans we may see some repeats of last night given Bennett's talents and the apparent inability of the Yankees to elevate contact against southpaws, but I also reserve the right to be surprised.

There are a couple changes to the lineup from last night, with Spencer Jones taking over in center field, Ali Sánchez behind the plate, and Amed Rosario starting at third and also batting third. I'm not sure any of those moves are necessarily upgrades from what the team had on Friday, but if they score more than one run it's all gravy.

articles.title: 4 fantasy football targets worth investing blind confidence in
articles.summary: These unproven players could lead you to fantasy football glory
articles.body:
Fantasy football drafts aren't won in Round 1. It's the picks you make later that define your team, along with the savvy waiver wire pickups you make along the way.

That means deviating from ADP in drafts, which is easier said than done. Nobody wants to be the person whose picks are mocked by their friends. It's a lot more fun to have a roster worth flaunting about, like Patrick Bateman flashing his business card to his highfalutin buddies in American Psycho .

Winning the draft, however, pales in comparison to winning a championship. So, have some gumption about your guys, even if it means taking them well before they were slated to go. And even if they haven't exactly proved worthy of their draft position yet.

We're highlighting four players who fit that second category, so here's a look at a group worth being blindly confident about in drafts.

Burden was incredible in limited snaps for Chicago last season, plus with DJ Moore and Olamide Zaccheaus gone, he's slated to be a full-time starting WR in Ben Johnson's explosive offense. While Burden is going as early as the fourth round despite a lack of production and a training camp groin injury, he has the talent to be a top-10 player at the position.

Fantasy football managers may be wary of rookie running backs after Ashton Jeanty and Omarion Hampton underwhelmed last season. Price, though, is worth taking another swing, as he very well could be the leading rusher for the reigning Super Bowl champions. Zach Charbonnet is coming off a torn ACLa and Kenneth Walker is on the Kansas City Chiefs, while Seattle invested a first-round pick in Price and clearly believes in him.

Kyle Shanahan has been known to make rookies work their way onto the field gradually, but Stribling's dominance in camp -- combined with injuries to Mike Evans and Ricky Pearsall, the latter of which is season-ending -- won't allow him to wait. Stribling has a chance to be San Francisco's top pass-catcher from Day 1, as he offers a strong 6-foot-2 frame and plenty of athletic ability after the catch.

A blazing fast running back who sat behind Travis Etienne Jr. last season, Tuten is expected to be the lead ball-carrier now, and Liam Coen could turn him into a fantasy football superstar. Chris Rodriguez could potentially steal goal line carries, but Tuten's immense athletic ability will make him difficult to take off the field in any situation. He's going much higher in drafts than his rookie year production would suggest, and he's worth the gamble.

With so much focus on whether former Giants star receiver Odell Beckham Jr. will make the team in his first year back on the roster since 2018, a receiver drafted a month after OBJ would traded is in danger of not surviving Sunday's cuts.

Paul Schwartz of the New York Post reports that Darius Slayton is on the bubble .

The report is bolstered by specific facts. First, Schwartz writes that Slayton is "clearly not moving the same" after surgery to repair a sports hernia. Second, Slayton played extensively in the preseason finale against the Jets — a game during which most of the obvious starters were held out.

Slayton stayed in the game even after quarterback Jameis Winston exited for Brandon Allen.

Slayton and Beckham, who possibly are competing for the same spot on the 53-man roster, played 33 snaps each. (Isaiah Hodgins and Dalen Cambre had 37 snaps each.)

A fifth-round pick in 2019, Slayton has appeared in 106 regular-season games with 78 starts in seven seasons. Last year, he signed a three-year, $36 million contract.

He's due to make $12.25 million in salary this year, with $500,000 in per-game active roster bonuses. A whopping $9.75 million of his salary is fully guaranteed.

Cutting him would leave behind a $12.75 million cap charge in 2026, with another $3 million applying in 2027.

A trade is also possible, in theory. The Giants surely would have to pay a significant portion of his guaranteed salary in order to make it happen.

The team's preseason depth chart continues to list Slayton as a starter, along with Malik Nabers.

articles.title: Dave Roberts reacts to concerning Shohei Ohtani development before Tigers game
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts gave an update superstar Shohei Ohtani's pitching status.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are 81-54 on the precipice of September, first place in the National League West and nine games up on the second-place San Diego Padres. They are in possession of the NL's No. 2 seed.

The Dodgers have done a lot of this winning despite some major injuries to their starting pitching staff. High-paid arms like Tyler Glasnow and Blake Snell have missed significant time, but did recently rejoin the staff.

Superstar two-way player Shohei Ohtani started the season on the mound, managing to stay healthy for the first half of the schedule. However, his last start came on July 3 and he has been out with injury since.

Apr 15, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers two-way player Shohei Ohtani pitches against the New York Mets in the first inning at Dodger Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The 32-year-old was supposed to make a start right before the All-Star break, but was scratched because of bicep and knee problems. Almost two months later, it has been left knee inflammation that has kept him off the mound.

Ohtani made 14 starts before injury, spinning 85 ⅔ innings. He is 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA, striking out 95 and walking 26. It was shaping up to be the best pitching season of his illustrious career.

He has not pitched in almost two months now, but it was reported earlier this week that Ohtani might return to the mound on Sunday at the Detroit Tigers. That hope has now been dashed by manager Dave Roberts' recent comments.

The fact that Ohtani might have got back in there Aug. 30 does suggest that he will pitch in September. At that, he should have enough time to build up for the postseason.

During this, the six-time All-Star has still been hitting. In 196 plate appearances since his last pitching appearance, he is slashing .274/.347/.560 (.907 OPS) with 12 home runs and 30 RBIs.

Those are of course elite numbers, but might leave something to be desired seeing as it is Ohtani. Perhaps this knee injury may be affecting him slightly on the hitting side. Even if he does not pitch Sunday, there is plenty of time for a ramp-up before the playoffs begin.

articles.title: North Dakota State Dominated FCS. Does That Predict Success In FBS?
articles.summary: North Dakota State and Sacramento State make the jump from FCS to FBS in 2026. Historical data shows which traits best predict immediate competitiveness at t...
articles.body:
Two programs make their FBS debuts today, and the betting market has very different expectations for them. North Dakota State opens its first FBS season at home against Jacksonville State. Despite being the newcomer, NDSU is a 6.5-point favorite. Sacramento State, which also moves up from FCS this year, opens at Eastern Michigan as a 9.5-point underdog.

That is a 17-point difference between two programs making the same formal jump in competition. Their recent histories in FCS competition help explain why. North Dakota State has spent more than a decade as the standard in FCS football. The Bison finished their 22-year FCS tenure with a 50-5 record in the playoffs , including 10 national championships. They went 12-1 last season before beginning the move to FBS. Sacramento State has also had strong seasons, including a 12-1 run to the FCS quarterfinals in 2022, but its recent results have been less consistent.

Both programs officially begin FBS competition in 2026 . North Dakota State joins the Mountain West as a football-only member, while Sacramento State joins the MAC. The question is whether their FCS records tell us much about what comes next.

How Five Year FCS Success Translates To First Year FBS Performance

To examine whether success at the FCS level carries over immediately to FBS, I first looked at established FCS programs that moved up since 2012 and had at least five seasons of history before playing their first full FBS schedule. Startup programs such as UTSA, Georgia State and Charlotte were excluded because they did not have five comparable FCS seasons.

For each program, I calculated its record over the five seasons immediately preceding its first full FBS season, then compared it with its record during Year 1 in FBS. The NCAA's realignment history confirms the recent additions to the group, including James Madison, Jacksonville State, Sam Houston, Kennesaw State, Delaware and Missouri State, followed by North Dakota State and Sacramento State in 2026.

In practical terms, teams that won more in FCS have done slightly better after moving up, on average. Their FCS record alone provides little certainty about how their first FBS season will unfold. The individual programs make that clear. James Madison had won 84.8% of its games over the five seasons before moving to FBS in 2022. The Dukes immediately went 8-3 and finished atop the Sun Belt East in their first season. Georgia Southern and Jacksonville State also transitioned well. Georgia Southern went 9-3 in its first FBS season, while Jacksonville State finished 9-4 in 2023.

Other successful FCS programs had a much harder time. Coastal Carolina had won 77.3% of its games during the five-year period before its first FBS season. The Chanticleers went 3-9 in 2017. Sam Houston presents an even stronger counterexample. The Bearkats had won more than 72% of their games during the five-year window and captured an FCS national championship before moving up. They finished 3-9 in their first full FBS season in 2023. Sam Houston's move also followed an unusual transition period that included the shortened spring 2021 season and a nine-game 2022 schedule.

A simple linear regression confirms the lack of strong predictive power. Five-year performance has a positive relationship with first-year FBS performance, but a weak one. Five-year winning percentage explains only about 5.4% of the variation in first-year FBS winning percentage, with a correlation of 0.23. The regression would place NDSU at roughly a .550 first-year FBS winning percentage and Sacramento State around .440 based on five-year record alone. Given how little variation the model explains, those numbers are better viewed as historical benchmarks than forecasts. Saturday will provide the first data point for both.

Predicting FBS Success From FCS Winning Percentage

A closer look at the historical transitions produced a much stronger signal than the five-year winning percentage alone. Two variables stood out:

Winning percentage in the program's final FCS season

Whether the program reached at least the FCS semifinals during the previous five seasons

A regression using those two factors explains 37.4% of the variation in first-year FBS winning percentage across the historical sample. The model estimates that every additional 10 percentage points of winning percentage in a team's final FCS season is associated with about 5.2 additional percentage points of first-year FBS winning percentage. Reaching at least an FCS semifinal during the preceding five years adds another 16.7 percentage points, holding final-season performance constant.

That model paints a particularly favorable picture for North Dakota State. The Bison finished their final FCS season 12-1, a .923 winning percentage, and easily satisfy the deep-playoff criterion after multiple championship and semifinal appearances over the previous five seasons. The model estimates a 71.6% first-year FBS winning percentage, equivalent to about 8.6 wins over a 12-game schedule.

Sacramento State enters with a different profile. The Hornets finished 2025 at 7-5, a .583 winning percentage, and did not reach an FCS semifinal during the five-year window. Their deepest postseason run was a quarterfinal appearance in 2022. The model estimates a 37.3% first-year FBS winning percentage, equivalent to about 4.5 wins.

The striking part is how closely those estimates line up with the betting market. Current season win totals list North Dakota State at 8.5 wins and Sacramento State at 4.5. A model built entirely from the recent FCS performance of previous programs making the jump arrives at essentially the same numbers. That agreement does not make the regression a substitute for the much broader information incorporated into betting markets. It does suggest that a program's performance immediately before moving up, combined with evidence of recent postseason success, captures a meaningful amount of its readiness to compete at the FBS level.

What FBS Conferences Should Look For In FCS Expansion Candidates

For FBS conferences evaluating potential new members, the key question may be which programs are positioned to compete at a high level immediately. In this small historical sample, the strongest signals were recent winning performance and deep FCS playoff success. North Dakota State checks both boxes, while Sacramento State enters with a more modest profile.

articles.title: Super League: Warrington seal home play-off spot as Wakefield also book post-season place
articles.summary: Warrington Wolves withstand late Hull FC fightback to win and guarantee home play-off; Wakefield Trinity beat York Knights to confirm their own post-season spot; watch round 26 of Super League from Thursday, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Sam Burgess's side looked to be cruising to a sixth straight win after back-to-back tries from Leon Hayes and Matty Ashton put them well in control towards the end of the first half.

The hosts had more than matched their opponents in the opening stages and looked set to reach the interval level after Warrington captain George Williams and Hull's Aidan Sezer traded early penalties, but hesitation under two high kicks cost the home side dear and Warrington went in 10 points clear.

When Josh Thewlis crossed for Warrington's third try 10 minutes into the second half it looked all over, but the Black and Whites, playing their last home game of the season, belatedly stirred.

Quick converted tries from Ethan O'Neill and Tom Briscoe, who is preparing to bring his 17-year career to a close, thrust them back into contention and left the visitors clinging on to seal a top-four slot.

Victory may also have come at a price for Warrington after Aaron Lindop failed a head injury assessment while Burgess lost both Luke Thomas and Joe Philbin to apparent leg injuries.

"We controlled the game for large parts, and I was a bit disappointed that they were able to score two tries towards the end," said Burgess, speaking to Sky Sports .

"I'm proud of them, they're a joy to coach. We're getting tough which is an important part of our journey - to be able to manage these periods and just get on with the job."

Hull FC head coach Andy Last praised his side's fighting spirit and paid tribute to Briscoe, who shared some emotional moments with the supporters after the final whistle.

"I'm disappointed with the results but I'm really proud of the performance," he said. "We were up against a really good team who are in good form, and we went toe to toe with them for 80 minutes.

"Tom Briscoe, a remarkable performance for him today, and great that he was able to score that try in front of the home fans."

Wakefield see off York to join Wolves in the play-offs

Wakefield came on strong in the second half to beat struggling York 28-12 and guarantee a place in the post-season play-offs.

Daryl Powell's side had to survive a scare as the visitors briefly hauled level early in the second period before tries from Jayden Myers, Max Jowitt and Lachlan Walmsley got the job done.

Corey Hall's converted try put the hosts in front early and after former Wakefield player Ben Jones-Bishop reduced the deficit, Walmsley grabbed his first to carve out a six-point half-time lead.

Mark Applegarth's side responded well and pulled level through a brilliant run by Xavier Va'a and Jon Bennison's subsequent conversion, but York's good work was undone when Myers barged over from Mike McMeeken's short pass.

Bennison's ball was then intercepted, allowing Jowitt to effectively seal the contest before Walmsley put the gloss on the win with his second late on.

The result was a welcome boost for Wakefield after three straight defeats and moves them two points clear in fourth place and six above seventh-placed St Helens, with their hopes of securing a home play-off tie likely to hinge on next week's visit of Warrington.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

articles.title: Egan Bernal sufre choque en Bogotá y taxista lo señala de retirarse del lugar sin responder
articles.standfirst: Polémica con Egan Bernal en Bogotá: taxista lo acusa de chocar su carro y huir de la escena
articles.summary: Polémica con Egan Bernal en Bogotá: taxista lo acusa de chocar su carro y huir de la escena
articles.body: El ciclista colombiano Egan Bernal, campeón del Tour de Francia 2019 y del Giro de Italia 2021, quedó en el centro de la polémica tras verse involucrado en un choque de tránsito en la Zona T, en el norte de Bogotá, mientras disfrutaba de sus vacaciones tras la temporada europea. De acuerdo con el testimonio brindado por el taxista afectado a medios de comunicación, el incidente consistió en un choque lateral entre su vehículo de servicio público y una camioneta de alta gama (Tesla) conducida por el pedalista zipaquireño. “Él empezó a discutir, a alegar, y yo le dije: ‘Al igual, yo voy por mi carril y por mi vía’. Lo que pasó es que él sacó el carro a la izquierda y lo mandó a la derecha y me le pegó al carro mío, yo no alcancé a frenar”, relató el taxista. El conductor señala que Bernal descendió brevemente del vehículo argumentando que "no había pasado nada" e intentó retomar la marcha. Ante los reclamos por el raspón y los daños materiales en el taxi, el deportista se habría retirado del lugar de los hechos. “Se bajó y dijo: ‘No, no pasó nada’ y se iba a volver a montar al carro, pero yo le dije: ‘No, sí pasó. Me responde porque usted me le pegó al carro’”, alega. El ciclista se dirigió hacia un parqueadero privado cercano, lugar hasta donde llegó el taxista acompañado por uniformados de la Policía Nacional. Los agentes de policía informaron que no podían ingresar ni intervenir en el procedimiento debido a que el vehículo ya se encontraba guardado dentro de una propiedad privada. El taxista implicado aclaró que su intención principal no es exigir una reparación económica por los daños del vehículo, sino recibir una disculpa pública o personal por la forma en que el deportista manejó la situación al retirarse del sitio. Además, el conductor señaló que uno de los acompañantes del vehículo presentó olor a alcohol, aunque enfatizó que no puede asegurar si Bernal se encontraba bajo los efectos del mismo. Hasta el momento, ni Egan Bernal ni los voceros de su equipo (Ineos Grenadiers) se han pronunciado públicamente sobre lo sucedido para ofrecer su versión del incidente. Se espera que en las próximas horas las autoridades de tránsito o el propio ciclista emitan un comunicado esclareciendo los hechos.

articles.title: Deportivo Pasto confirmó la salida de Jonathan Risueño con un frío comunicado
articles.standfirst: Jonathan Risueño deja de ser el técnico del Deportivo Pasto tras un flojo arranque en Liga
articles.summary: Jonathan Risueño deja de ser el técnico del Deportivo Pasto tras un flojo arranque en Liga
articles.body: El ciclo de Jonathan Risueño como director técnico del Deportivo Pasto ha llegado a su fin. La derrota por 0-1 en casa frente a Llaneros —la quinta caída consecutiva del equipo en el semestre— terminó por detonar la salida del estratega español, poniendo punto final a una etapa tumultuosa en el fútbol profesional colombiano. Sin embargo, el desenlace no estuvo exento de extrañeza: el club nariñense optó por no emitir un comunicado directo confirmando de forma explícita la rescisión de su contrato. En su lugar, la institución publicó un sobrio mensaje informando únicamente que René Rosero asumirá como director técnico interino, con la asistencia de Wilson Morelo. Esta omisión sobre la desvinculación de Risueño apuntaría a resguardarse de eventuales implicaciones legales en la liquidación del contrato. La llegada de Risueño a la capital nariñense a comienzos de año tuvo momentos positivos. En la Liga BetPlay 2026-I, el entrenador logró clasificar al Deportivo Pasto a la fase de cuartos de final, firmando actuaciones competitivas. No obstante, el rendimiento del plantel sufrió un desplome drástico para el segundo semestre, registrando cero puntos de 15 posibles en las primeras cinco fechas. En total, el paso de Jonathan Risueño por el Deportivo Pasto dejó las siguientes cifras: Más allá de los balances en el terreno de juego, el paso de Risueño estuvo signado por continuos episodios disciplinarios y una relación distante con la prensa y las hinchadas rivales: Con la salida del entrenador español, la junta directiva del Deportivo Pasto encomendó la conducción del primer equipo a René Rosero. El exfutbolista del club, un hombre de la casa con experiencia previa en interinatos, asumirá la urgencia de enderezar el rumbo en la Liga BetPlay y sacar al cuadro volcánico de los puestos bajos de la tabla de posiciones.

articles.title: “Pensaba cosas feas”: De la depresión a héroe de Santa Fe, la lección de vida de Franco Fagúndez
articles.standfirst: Franco Fagúndez confiesa su lucha contra la depresión tras la clasificación de Santa Fe ante River Plate
articles.summary: Franco Fagúndez confiesa su lucha contra la depresión tras la clasificación de Santa Fe ante River Plate
articles.body: La noche en que Independiente Santa Fe logró una histórica clasificación a los cuartos de final de la Copa Sudamericana tras vencer a River Plate en Buenos Aires, el verdadero triunfo no fue solo deportivo. La gran figura del encuentro, el atacante uruguayo Franco Fagúndez, aprovechó los micrófonos pospartido para entregar una desgarradora y esperanzadora lección de resiliencia y salud mental. Fagúndez disputó ante River Plate un partido consagratorio. Enfrentando a defensores de jerarquía internacional como Nicolás Otamendi y Lucas Martínez Quarta, el uruguayo generó peligro constante atacando los espacios. El momento cumbre llegó al minuto 80: Santa Fe caía y necesitaba un gol para no quedar eliminado de la competencia continental. Con la presión de más de 80.000 espectadores en contra, Fagúndez asumió la responsabilidad de cobrar un penal decisivo. Con total serenidad envió el balón al fondo de la red, empató el partido y forzó la definición desde el punto penal, donde el conjunto 'Cardenal' terminó sellando su tiquete a la siguiente fase. Más allá de su gesta futbolística, las palabras de Fagúndez al término del compromiso conmovieron al mundo del fútbol. El charrúa reveló la profunda crisis personal que atravesó tan solo un año atrás: "Yo pasé muchas cosas hace un año, tuve depresión, no fue un año bueno, me rompí la rodilla y era complicado. Hoy justo pensé en eso: el fútbol es muy lindo. Pensaba cosas feas, me subía al auto y a veces tenía ganas de darme contra algo... un amigo murió y, además, problemas familiares me hacen darle las gracias a Dios por lo que vivo en este momento". El delantero explicó que durante sus días más oscuros, enfocarse en el trabajo diario y estar presente en cada entrenamiento se convirtió en su refugio para despejar la mente. Esa misma fortaleza mental para superar batallas personales fue la que le permitió pararse en la cancha de River Plate sin temor alguno. El testimonio de Franco Fagúndez trasciende la cancha. En un entorno deportivo donde a menudo se exige hipercompetitividad y resistencia emocional absoluta, el jugador de Santa Fe hizo un llamado urgente a romper los estigmas sobre la depresión y el bienestar emocional: "Debes buscar ayuda; solo no puedes." El paso de Fagúndez por el Monumental dejó una huella que va más allá de un penal anotado o una clasificación continental: fue la muestra de cómo el acompañamiento adecuado y la resiliencia pueden transformar los momentos más difíciles en triunfos de vida.

articles.title: Charlotte Henshaw wins 12th Para-canoe world title 11 days after being in hospital with cellulitis
articles.summary: Britain's Charlotte Henshaw has won her 12th Para-canoe World Championship title - less than two weeks after being in hospital with cellulitis.
articles.body:
Britain's Charlotte Henshaw has won her 12th Para-canoe World Championship title - less than two weeks after being in hospital with cellulitis.

The 39-year-old contracted the condition - usually a bacterial infection which makes the skin painful, hot and swollen - in her leg and, after leaving hospital, was unable to train on the water in the lead up to the championships in Poznan, Poland.

But in Saturday's KL2 200m final she crossed the finish line more than three seconds ahead of the rest of the field for her eighth world title in the event, adding to the four she has won in the VL3 equivalent.

"Of all the titles I've managed to win, that probably means the most because I did not know I was going to be here a week ago," she said.

"There's maybe something to be said for taking the pressure off and going out and trusting my body and my experience.

"I've been competing at the highest level for an awfully long time and in moments where things aren't going well and the preparation gets swept out from underneath you, you have to draw on every single bit of experience.

"Eleven days ago, I didn't think I would be on the plane so to come here and compete and then retain my title, I couldn't be happier and it means a lot this one."

A double leg amputee, Henshaw is a three-time Paralympic champion in Para-canoeing since switching from swimming in 2017.

Writing on Instagram , external after her heat on Friday, Henshaw said: "The last week or so has definitely put things into perspective.

"It's so easy to get caught up in results, rankings, times and expectations, but when your long-term limb health becomes the priority, those things seem a lot less important."

Elsewhere in Poznan on Saturday, Henshaw's team-mate Hope Gordon won gold in the KL3 200m while Stuart Wood won bronze in the men's VL3 event.

For Gordon, who last month represented Scotland in Para-powerlifting at the Commonwealth Games, it is a first KL3 world title - having previously won two in the VL3.

articles.title: 2026 Little League World Series: Curaçao's Jaymiëll Martina strikes out 12 in 4-0 win over Japan for international championship
articles.summary: Four errors by Japan in the third inning led to three runs, giving Martina all the runs he needed to win.
articles.body:
The 2026 Little League World Series is down to its final games with the international and United States titles to be determined on Saturday, and those winners playing for the LLWS World Series championship on Sunday at Howard J. Lamade Stadium in Williamsport, Pennsylvania.

Pitcher Jaymiëll Martina notched 12 strikeouts to lead Curaçao (Willemstad) to a 4-0 win over Japan (Tokyo) for the LLWS international championship.

Japan threatened to score early on singles by Tensei Yazawa and Yunosuke Yabe to lead off the game. Martina then walked Kei Kawanishi to load the bases. But Martina struck out Ryosuke Takaoka and Taiga Yumitori to keep Japan off the board.

Yunosuke Yabe didn't allow a hit in his first two innings for Tokyo. But Curaçao broke through with three runs in the third, thanks to several defensive miscues by Japan.

Jaymiel Antonia reached base on a dropped third strike by catcher Kei Kawanishi. Nathanael Jansen then laid down a bunt to move Antonia over, but Yazawa made an error throwing the ball to second base. Center fielder Takeru Yorozu then threw the ball wide of third base, allowing Antonia to score.

Jansen advanced to third on a sacrifice bunt, then came in to score on a bunt by Jordan Richards and an error by first baseman Rui Tobata. Curaçao added its third run when Tobata fielded another bunt and threw wide of first base, allowing Richards to score.

Curaçao will face the winner of the U.S. championship game between Henderson, Nevada (Mountain region) and Hamilton, Ohio (Great Lakes) on Sunday.

The LLWS schedule and results leading up to Saturday and Sunday's championship games can be seen here .

articles.title: Cody Gakpo transfer news: Manchester City open talks to sign Liverpool forward
articles.summary: Man City allowed wide forwards Savio and Omar Marmoush to join Tottenham this month, and winger Jack Grealish is of interest to Everton and Sunderland; Liverpool are set to sign winger Bradley Barcola and added Victor Munoz earlier this summer
articles.body:
Liverpool will be considering their situation given contact has come late in the window.

One source told Sky Sports News a potential move for the winger is advancing in Manchester City's direction amid the interest of Tottenham.

Discussions are also under way over personal terms for the Netherlands international.

Liverpool are on the verge of signing Bradley Barcola from PSG for £106m rising to £123m, while Victor Munoz arrived from Osasuna earlier this summer.

Manchester City allowed Savio and Omar Marmoush to join Tottenham earlier month, reducing Enzo Maresca's options on the wing.

City did not name a single winger on their bench in Friday's win over Crystal Palace and started with Phil Foden - who Enzo Maresca admitted is not a winger - out wide at Selhurst Park.

Jack Grealish is of interest to Everton and Sunderland - he is believed to prefer a return to the Toffees - and was absent against Palace, further reducing their options in that area.

Spurs also targeted Gakpo in this window before signing Savio and Marmoush.

Andoni Iraola was non-committal over Gakpo's future on Saturday after Liverpool's home draw against Nottingham Forest .

Gakpo claimed the assist for Alexander Isak's goal at Anfield, after which Iraola told TNT : "Now we have two or three days and we will see what happens with everyone.

"I'm looking forward to arriving at September 2 and knowing what squad we have.

"It's true we created both goals from the right side and they were very good goals."

Bradley Barcola is set to sign a Liverpool contract to 2031 after the Premier League club reached an agreement with Paris Saint-Germain over the structure of the transfer.

The final discussions had centred over the structure of deal, with Liverpool now set to pay £106m up front and up to £17m in add-ons.

Documents must still be exchanged between the clubs and Barcola must complete a medical.

There had been a gap in valuation between the two clubs earlier in the summer, with PSG previously asking for around £145m for the France international, but the 23-year-old is now set to sign a five-year deal with Andoni Iraola's side.

Barcola would become Liverpool's second most expensive signing of all time, following the club-record deal to sign Alexander Isak from Newcastle for £125m last summer.

Liverpool are also trying to sign a second new winger, with their target currently Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr following difficult negotiations with Brighton for Yankuba Minteh.

articles.title: WATCH: Simone Biles left blushing as Indiana Fever fans deliver special tribute
articles.summary: Simone Biles was left blushing and beaming with pride after receiving a special tribute from Indiana Fever fans during Friday night’s game against the Connec...
articles.body:
Simone Biles was left blushing and beaming with pride after receiving a special tribute from Indiana Fever fans during Friday night's game against the Connecticut Sun.

The 11-time Olympic medallist was in attendance at Gainbridge Fieldhouse when the Fever decided to honour the gymnastics legend in front of the home crowd.

Biles appeared on the giant screen during the game, immediately prompting a huge reaction from the crowd.

The legendary gymnast smiled and waved as the fans continued to cheer for her, creating a special moment for one of the greatest athletes of all time.

The Fever also shared a video of the heartwarming reception on their X handle, celebrating Biles with a simple message:

"a moment for the G.O.A.T. Simone Biles," Fever wrote.

The tribute clearly meant a lot to Biles, who could be seen smiling and acknowledging the fans as the arena erupted around her.

It was a fitting reception for Biles, who has spent much of her career performing in front of packed arenas and receiving recognition for her achievements in gymnastics.

This time, however, she was not the one competing.

Instead, Biles was enjoying the action from the stands when the Fever made sure the spotlight found her.

The reception was not the only memorable interaction Biles had with the Fever during her visit.

Following the game, the gymnast made her way towards the area outside the Fever locker room, where she met several members of the team.

Biles shared hugs and smiles with Indiana players, including Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell, Lexie Hull and Aliyah Boston.

She also received an enthusiastic welcome from Sophie Cunningham, who greeted the gymnastics legend warmly.

For Biles, the night offered a chance to experience the kind of admiration she has so often received throughout her own career from a different perspective.

articles.title: 44 Colts who are locks to make initial 53-man roster
articles.summary: With roster cutdown day looming, how many Indianapolis Colts players are locks to make the team?
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts' initial 53-man roster must be set by 6:00 PM ET on Sunday. While there will be some tough decisions for GM Chris Ballard to make, the roster is already largely set.

After putting together one final roster projection , here are the players at each position that we view as roster locks heading into cutdown day.

I fully expect Anthony Richardson to be on the Colts this year, but I suppose there's still a small chance a deal is made.

McGowan emerged as RB2, while DJ Giddens and Ulysses Bentley are competing for the RB3 role.

Treadwell played just six snaps in the preseason finale -- he's a roster lock. Deion Burks, Coleman Owen, and Anthony Gould are competing for one spot, while Nick Westbrook-Ikhine may be on the outside looking in.

Mallory's impact in the passing game this summer secured his roster spot.

Farmer will be the first guard off the bench and Tenuta the first tackle. Dalton Tucker probably makes the team, but his snapping was so shaky this summer that his spot on the team shouldn't be guaranteed.

Jaylahn Tuimoloau is likely on the team, but he did play 35 snaps in the preseason finale -- the fifth-most on the team -- after having a rocky summer.

Neither Jerry Tillery nor Derrick Nnadi may end up on the team after quiet preseasons.

What playing time and the depth chart look like may not be known, but it feels safe to say that these five players will make up the Colts' linebacker room.

I do think that Johnathan Edwards makes the team because of his special teams abilities, but the depth of this position group was exposed in the preseason.

Jonathan Owens will be a core special teams contributor for the Colts.

I do think that Spencer Shrader secured the Colts' kicking job in the preseason finale, but we'll leave the door open for the Colts to name Blake Grupe the winner, as he did have the stronger overall performance this summer.

articles.title: Bills release once-promising 49ers 2nd-round pick as final cuts begin
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers had a 2018 second-round pick who looked like a budding star, now he's being released by his fifth NFL team.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills on Saturday announced a handful of their final cuts as they trim their roster to 53 players. Among their initial cuts was former San Francisco 49ers second-round pick Dante Pettis.

Pettis was the 49ers' second-round pick in the 2018 draft. He put together a strong rookie campaign in San Francisco with 27 catches for 467 yards and five touchdowns despite suffering a knee injury in Week 4 and being limited to 12 games. His arrow was pointed up with the 49ers and it looked after Year 1 like he might be a foundational piece of their receiving corps.

Unfortunately for Pettis, the wheels came off in 2019 as the 49ers became a Super Bowl contender. He caught 11 balls for 109 yards and two touchdowns in 11 games during his sophomore campaign. Pettis didn't make it through 2020 with the 49ers. He didn't record a catch in five games and was waived in November.

Since being waived he's been unable to catch on with a substantial role on any club. He played five games across one-plus seasons with the New York Giants. He had one year with the Chicago Bears in 2022, didn't sign with anyone in 2023, and then caught on with the New Orleans Saints for the 2024 and 2025 seasons. The Buffalo Bills signed him this offseason and he wasn't able to earn a place on the 53-man roster.

Pettis since his rookie season has 65 catches for 764 yards and eight touchdowns in 54 games with 12 starts.

This offseason, Buffalo signed Logue to a reserves/futures contract. Logue is a candidate to land on the Bills' practice squad.

Last season, Logue appeared in three games with the Bills. He posted 1/2 sack, two tackles and a pass defended.

The Bills signed Logue off the Atlanta Falcons' practice squad during the 2024 NFL season. The Falcons originally drafted Logue in the sixth-round of the 2024 NFL draft. Back as a rookie in 2024, Logue had a similar role in Buffalo. He appeared in two games for the Bills and recorded a pair of tackles.

Logue was one of 13 players Buffalo released ahead of the roster cut deadline. The Bills also released former Georgia receiver Mecole Hardman, who scored the winning touchdown in Super Bowl 58.

articles.title: Ravens release Chris Moore after impressive preseason finale
articles.summary: The Ravens released veteran receiver Chris Moore despite his productive performance in Baltimore’s preseason finale against Washington
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens have released veteran wide receiver Chris Moore as they continue reducing their roster, according to Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic . Moore delivered one of Baltimore's best offensive performances during its 41-3 preseason victory over the Washington Commanders . He caught three passes for a game-high 54 yards during the opening possession, including a contested 25-yard touchdown from Tyler Huntley.

The performance provided a final reminder of the dependable depth Moore can offer, but Baltimore's investment in several young receivers made his path to the initial roster difficult.

Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman lead the group, while Ja'Kobi Lane, Elijah Sarratt, Devontez Walker and LaJohntay Wester entered the final weekend with strong cases for roster positions. Keeping Moore would have required the Ravens to carry seven receivers or expose one of their younger players to waivers.

Moore, 33, began his career with Baltimore after being selected in the fourth round of the 2016 NFL draft. He spent five seasons with the Ravens before playing for Houston, Tennessee, Arizona and Washington. He returned to Baltimore shortly before training camp.

Because Moore is a vested veteran, he immediately becomes a free agent and does not have to pass through waivers. Zrebiec reported that Moore would be a strong practice-squad candidate if he is interested in remaining with the organization.

The move creates room for Baltimore's young receivers while leaving open the possibility that Moore could return as an experienced reserve, special-teams contributor and trusted insurance option.

articles.title: ‘There’s Like 12 People at This USC Home Opener,’ ‘Everyone Must Be Stuck in LA Traffic’ — CFB World Rips Trojans’ ‘Pathetic’ Turnout vs. SJSU
articles.summary: Week 0 of the college football season is finally here, but fans of the USC Trojans and San Jose State Spartans must not have gotten the memo. USC opened up i...
articles.body:
Week 0 of the college football season is finally here, but fans of the USC Trojans and San Jose State Spartans must not have gotten the memo.

USC opened up its 2026 season against a familiar foe at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, but in a rather less-than-packed stadium. While the Coliseum is typically full of Trojan fans up to the nosebleeds, the empty stadium stood out immediately at the start of the game, especially given the heavy anticipation for USC's season.

This quickly became a topic of conversation on social media as analysts, media personalities, and college football fans began poking fun at the empty stands.

College Football World Reacts to USC's Empty Stands

"Ain't nobody at this USC game. That's pathetic even when your team not playing a top opponent you show up and leave at halftime," wrote a user on X.

PFN Analyst Alec Elijah, who was at the game, shared a photo of the stadium and exclaimed, "Everyone must be stuck in LA traffic."

On3's Brooks Austin took to his X account and cracked a joke about how many fans were in attendance: "There's like 12 people at this USC home opener."

"USC should build a Northwestern-like stadium that seats 30,000 people. Seeing every home game ever at 20% capacity is depressing," they wrote.

Others tried to look for reasons for the limited turnout. It's no secret that California is in the midst of a major heat wave as the back end of summer wraps up.

During the game, temperatures reached the low 90s, which may have contributed to low attendance at the start of the season, despite the lowest ticket price being just $9.

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

When ticket prices dropped, USC beat writer Ryan Kartje argued that the biggest reason for the low ticket sales is the California heat.

"The reason people aren't clamoring to be in the upper rows of the Coliseum tomorrow isn't *Lincoln Riley and USC* it's the stifling, triple-digit heat," he wrote .

Of course, other fan bases weren't buying this excuse, as several teams play in the blistering heat.

"USC beat writer says Trojan fans won't show up to the season opener because it's hot outside. El. Oh. El." said Oklahoma Sooners radio host Travis J Davidson .

It's worth noting that the Trojans announced before the game that their top receivers, Tanook Hines and Terrell Anderson, would be out for Saturday's outing for "injury precaution."

Perhaps the fact that the Trojans were resting some key players also lowered fans' excitement for the game.

Still, for a team that's ranked in the top-15 and has College Football Playoff aspirations, you would expect the stadium to be packed for the season opener like it was a Saturday night against an SEC opponent.

articles.title: Erasmus relieved the pressure flipped onto Rennie after tying Springboks-All Blacks series
articles.summary: South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus was looking forward to watching New Zealand counterpart Dave Rennie squirm for the next week after tying their four-test se...
articles.body:
CAPE TOWN, South Africa (AP) — South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus was looking forward to watching New Zealand counterpart Dave Rennie squirm for the next week after tying their four-test series on Saturday.

The Springboks relied on a masterclass of goalkicking by Cheslin Kolbe — seven from seven off the tee — to win the second test 33-26 after New Zealand outscored them on tries 4-3.

World champion South Africa dropped the first test in Johannesburg and hasn't lost consecutive tests at home on Erasmus' watch — since 2018 — and he was relieved they got back into a series in which they started as the heavy favorite.

"Of course I felt the pressure, and the players will tell you I felt the pressure. I try not to put it on them but I was nervous," Erasmus said.

He noted he and the older Rennie were November babies, both Scorpios, and quipped: "That's why he's able to work me out.

"It's his first loss (as All Blacks coach) ... and he'll feel what we felt this week.

"We 100% understand why people are upset because no one wants to support a losing team. No one in South Africa wants to support anything that's not working. A loss here and there doesn't make you a losing team immediately, but it's when you go on a losing run that the pressure comes on.

"We must make sure we're not confident and think we're all good again because there were a lot of things we didn't do well."

One of the reasons Rennie was hired in March was because predecessor Scott Robertson had a 1-3 record against South Africa. Erasmus believed the All Blacks were "two classes up" from last year.

"They're really well coached and they've got athletes who can beat you on a dime," he said. "A couple of more phases at the end and it could have been a draw."

He explained the late switch of the front rows was because of the weather. They expected wet conditions but they turned out dry so he went with the lighter front row in the reserves. They were still a few kilograms heavier than New Zealand's starters.

Fullback Damian Willemse, a key playmaker who can cover midfield and flyhalf, injured a hamstring and Erasmus wasn't counting on him for the third test in Soweto next Saturday.

Rennie reported a clean bill of health apart from a neck issue for winger Will Jordan, who finished the match.

He described their lineout issues as "a work on" and thought the scrummaging, an issue in the first test, was reasonably managed by referee Angus Gardner but claimed the Springboks were still walking around and coming through the tighthead.

Erasmus called it "nonsense" and Boks loosehead Ox Nché said there were no complications: "We wasted a lot of time in scrums today because we all had different interpretations."

articles.title: Packers waive DB Travion Fluellen to make room for Jonnu Smith
articles.summary: Free agent tight end Jonnu Smith agreed to a one-year deal with the Packers earlier this week.
articles.body:
Free agent tight end Jonnu Smith agreed to a one-year deal with the Packers earlier this week. Smith signed his deal on Saturday, and the Packers needed to make room.

In a corresponding move, the Packers waived defensive back Travion Fluellen, the team announced.

Fluellen signed with the Packers on Aug. 11.

Fluellen played collegiately at Houston Baptist for one season before transferring to Middle Tennessee State.

In three seasons at Middle Tennessee State, he played 36 games and recorded 197 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss, one sack, five interceptions and 16 pass breakups. As a senior in 2023, he ended the season ranked third on the team with 64 tackles, including 2.5 stops for loss, a team-high three interceptions and three pass breakups.

Fluellen went undrafted in 2024, signing with the Saints as a college free agent.

Fluellen spent the final five weeks of the 2024 season on the Saints' practice squad, but he did not appear in a game. The Saints signed him to a futures contract after the season.

New Orleans waived him in June 2025, and he was not signed elsewhere last year.

articles.title: Sox shut out Yankees in Game 1, 6-0
articles.summary: The Sox take the season series lead against the Yankees
articles.body:
The Sox jumped out to a sweet, sweet lead in the first with Wilyer Abreu's twenty-third home run, a career high.

Jake Bennett went 1-2-3 in the bottom of the inning and damn it felt good. He did the same in the second. He threw a fantastic game, in fact, keeping the Yankees off-balance and off the board.

Carlos Rodon who, outside of Abreu's homer, had been extremely steady, unraveled in the fifth inning: a long at-bat to Adley Rutschman, a small tantrum after a passed ball that scored Rutschman, followed by a walk and a hit-by-pitch. Simply put, the Sox tilted him and got to the Yankees' bullpen early with the bases loaded. Unfortunately, nothing came of it, and the insurance run had to be enough to satisfy…for now. 2-0, Sox.

But this rush to the bullpen could take on more importance in Game 2 of the doubleheader tonight. Yankees manager Aaron Boone used four pitchers by the seventh inning and was pretty liberal with the use of the bench too. We'll see how fresh the Yankees feel later on.

Garrett Whitlock returned from the IL in the eighth and in the same inning, Rutschman successfully used an ABS challenge to recover a strikeout (he did it again in the ninth too). What began as a tough game for Rutschman ultimately was a triumph: ending his drought at the plate, scoring two runs, and converting those strikeouts.

Nick Sogard was unfairly sent back to second base in the fifth inning when the third-base umpire inexplicably called time while the play was still in progress. He was sent back and forth from third to second and back while it was sorted out. He had a nice game.

Three Yankees let a shallow outfield fly drop among them and it was glorious.

Yankees fans booed the team and started leaving the stadium. Also glorious.

The Sox had several defensive hiccups but they had some great defensive plays too.

The Sox took a one-game lead against the Yankees in the season series. This series is the last time they'll meet in the regular season and for the record, I completely disagree; what is September without the Red Sox/Yankees?

Jake Bennett was in command today: 6 IP, 3H, 0 BB, 7K. Garrett Whitlock returned, with a 1-2-3 eighth inning, and only 13 pitches. Tyron Guerrero and Jovani Moran also did their jobs. No Yankees batters walked.

Erik Miller and Aroldis Chapman remain fresh for Game 2 tonight.

Lots of heads-up running to capitalize on Yankees passed balls, errors, miscues, falls in the outfield. I love our running game.

The Sox added four runs and we could relax.

I hate to get picky on a day like this but here goes.

He had 3K, though also some nice moments over at first. Tough day at the plate.

A throwing error by Caleb Durbin, and a fielding error by Eli White. Ceddanne Rafaela uncharacteristically misread what looked like an easy fly and allowed it by him (though he recovered quickly from his initial misplay and started a beautiful relay to the plate that erased the runner and kept the Yankees off the board). Adley Rutschman allowed a passed ball in the fifth, and also dropped a foul tip, seemingly while trying to transfer the ball in order to throw it to third (there was no reason for this). This gave the Yankees another bite at the apple but thankfully nothing came of it. A parade of miscues and two actual errors; that's not usually the Sox brand of ball. This being said, there were some nice scoops at first, and the dramatic recovery to nail the runner at the plate could almost make you forget about the rest (except for the box score, which doesn't lie). But with a dramatic finish and the W, all is forgiven.

Andrew Monasterio's single in the ninth drove in two and instantly turned a relatively tight 2-0 game into a shout-out-loud party. The Sox had no outs and went on to score two more in the inning but this was the play that wrapped the game up in a bow.

articles.title: Charley North, former OU football assistant coach and OCA Hall of Famer, dies at 82
articles.summary: Charley North died Aug. 25. He was 82. A longtime football coach at the collegiate and high school level, North was best known for his work on Barry Switzer’...
articles.body:
Legendary football coach Charley North died Aug. 25. He was 82.

A longtime coach at the collegiate and high school level, North was best known for his work on Barry Switzer 's staff at OU . He also coached at Arkansas, Alabama, Texas A&M and TCU.

He also coached at Wagoner — his alma mater — along with Tecumseh and Dibble. He finished his coaching career volunteering as an assistant at Norman High School, where he coached his grandson.

North spent more than four decades coaching football. He was inducted into the Oklahoma Coaches Association Hall of Fame in 2013 .

North was an all-state football and baseball selection at Wagoner High school.

After playing football at Panhandle State, North returned to Wagoner in 1967 to begin his coaching career. His first head coach job was at Tecumseh in 1972 and then McAlester in 1976. He joined OU in 1979, working under Switzer and Gary Gibbs.

He bookended his coaching career taking over Dibble High School and then coaching his grandson.

Funeral services have been set for 10 a.m. Friday, Sept. 4, at the NPS Center for Arts and Learning in Norman.

articles.title: Patriots pull off trade before 53-man roster cut deadline
articles.summary: The Patriots added to their running back room on Saturday by reportedly acquiring Corey Kiner in a trade.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots announced on Saturday that they have acquired former Arizona Cardinals running back Corey Kiner in a trade . According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the Patriots sent a 2028 seventh-round draft pick to the Cardinals in exchange for Kiner.

The corresponding move, per the Patriots, was the team releasing running back Hassan Haskins.

Kiner will have a chance to step in as the No. 3 option at running back behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. The former undrafted free agent out of Cincinnati had 39 carries for 180 rushing yards and two touchdowns, averaging 4.6 yards per carry during the preseason.

He has spent time with the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings' practice squad.

The Patriots came into training camp with a talented offensive backfield, including Lan Larison, Jam Miller and Terrell Jennings. The additions of Haskins and JaMycal Hasty spiced things up a bit.

Kiner gives the Patriots another slasher on the ground to fill the depth void in New England's offensive backfield for the 2026 season.

articles.title: Former Lions cornerback Terrion Arnold officially signs with Seahawks
articles.summary: Arnold will not count against the 53-man roster while he is on the commissioner’s exempt list.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks have officially signed former Detroit Lions cornerback, Terrion Arnold. It was announced earlier this month that Arnold would be joining Seattle . However, considering the off the field issues that Arnold is dealing with ( eight felony charges, including armed robbery and kidnapping ), there remained questions as to the exact timing of his signing – or whether he would sign at all. Well now, those questions can officially go to rest.

It was also announced that once the league receives Arnold's contract from Seattle, that he will be placed on the commissioner's exempt list . While on this list, Arnold will be paid, however he cannot practice or play. As long as Arnold is on the commissioner's exempt list, he will not count against the Seahawks 53-man roster .

The Seahawks have had questions about their depth at the cornerback position this training camp. Those questions remained even after the news of Arnold joining Seattle earlier this month. Perhaps that is what led the team to sign another veteran cornerback, Trevon Diggs. The signing of Diggs, as well as Arnold going on the exempt list, makes Saturday's signing appear to be a move for later on in the season and perhaps after 2026.

For those curious about the timing of this signing, and why the Seahawks waited so long, ESPN's Brady Henderson explains it well . Arnold would count against the 91-man roster for at least one day, until he's placed on the commissioner's exempt list. Since he would be unable to practice or play in any games (including preseason), it made more sense for Seattle to leave that roster spot available for someone who could practice and play. This means that it would make sense for Seattle to make this move after the preseason games finished up, but before the 53-man roster cut down day. In other words, today.

To make room on their roster, the Seahawks released offensive tackle, Derrick Graham.

articles.title: Stephen Curry’s multimillion-dollar decision puts Warriors’ next era under the microscope
articles.summary: Stephen Curry’s future with the Golden State Warriors is now officially in his hands. The extension window opened on Saturday, and the four-time champion can...
articles.body:
Stephen Curry's future with the Golden State Warriors is now officially in his hands. The extension window opened on Saturday, and the four-time champion can sign up to two more years worth $136.7 million.

The Warriors have made clear they will give their star whatever he wants. The question is what Curry decides to do with that power.

There is a lot riding on it, and not just for him.

'What the terms of a new extension look like for Curry will be completely up to him, as the Warriors are prepared to offer their star whatever he wants,' NBA insider Brett Siegel wrote. 'If Steph wants the full $136.7 million through the 2028-29 season, he will get that. If he wants to take a discount to help the team, GM Mike Dunleavy Jr. will have no problem with said deal.'

The timing matters as much as the money. ESPN's Bobby Marks laid out the terms: 'From now until June 30, Curry is eligible to sign up to a two-year/$136.7M extension. Because of the Over 38 rule, 2 years is the maximum allowed in an extension. He can sign for up to 3 seasons if he waits until FA.'

If Curry signs immediately, it locks the Warriors into a difficult financial spot. If he waits, the picture changes completely.

Brian Windhorst has argued that waiting may be the smartest move.

'If he chooses to sign right now, he could get two years at $140 million,' Windhorst said.

'Obviously if that's what he says he wants, you give it to him. But if he doesn't sign his contract extension right now the Warriors could have over $100 million in salary cap space next summer.'

That is the heart of the decision. Sign now and secure the bag. Wait, and give Golden State the flexibility to build a proper contender around him before he retires.

The roster as it stands is not championship calibre, and Curry has made clear he still wants to compete for titles.

The Warriors want him for life, and the belief is that he wants the same. But between a max deal and a deliberate pause lies the entire future of the franchise's next era.

Everyone will be watching what he does with the pen.
