articles.title: Reports: After Franck Kessié deal falls through, Juventus in talks with Spurs for Pape Matar Sarr
articles.summary: As one midfielder goes elsewhere, a new one becomes an option in Juventus’ search for more depth.
articles.body:
For the second time this summer, Juventus' directors have dialed up Tottenham Hotspur in an attempt to bring somebody in and solve a very urgent problem.

First it was in goal, now it's in midfield thanks to Juve's potential deal for Franck Kessié — who has sicne returned to Atalanta after leaving Bergamo a decade ago — fell through earlier in the day on Saturday.

According to multiple reports out of Italy, Juventus are in talks with Tottenham over a loan move for Pape Matar Sarr, the 23-year-old midfielder from Senegal who is on his way out of the London-based club before the end of the summer transfer window. We know that because Spurs manager Roberto De Zerbi confirmed that Sarr was one of a handful of players who will leave the club before next weekend's deadline. Juventus want to sign Sarr with the same kind of terms that they brought Guglielmo Vicario to Turin on — a season-long loan deal with an option to buy next summer.

Sarr doesn't lack for interested clubs, with Nottingham Forest, Monaco and Besiktas reportedly interested in him as well. Juventus and Tottenham are reportedly set for more talks at some point late Saturday and likely into Sunday considering how this looks to be developing.

With Tottenham focusing a good amount of their massive spending this summer on trying to improve the midfield — not like it's worked all that well based on their first two Premier League games, though … — it's only natural that somebody will have to exit the building as a result. And, as Tottenham try to scramble to make other things happen on the market, Sarr is clearly one of those players who can see the writing on the wall.

Sarr played in 23 games in the Premier League last season, totaling just under 1,400 minutes and recording two goals and four assists for a Tottenham squad that was both ravaged by injuries and just a total mess no matter who their manager was at the time. Sarr has been with Tottenham since 2021 when he signed from French side Metz on a deal that initially cost in the neighborhood of €15 million.

With Kessié heading to Atalanta, it's pretty obvious that the club is now just going to target a depth option that is likely much more affordable rather than somebody who could challenge for big-time starting minutes. Who knows if that's the right way to go — especially with Khephren Thuram's status looking more and more uncertain — but this team needs cover in the midfield before the summer mercato ends, and apparently Sarr is next up on the list as his exit from Tottenham looks like a mere certainty.

articles.title: Serie A | Juventus 2-0 Parma: Nico Gonzalez inspirational
articles.summary: Nico Gonzalez came off the bench and sparked Juventus into life for a 2-0 victory over Parma, scoring one and instigating another for Teun Koopmeiners, but J...
articles.body:
Nico Gonzalez came off the bench and sparked Juventus into life for a 2-0 victory over Parma, scoring one and instigating another for Teun Koopmeiners, but Jonathan David was jeered.

The Bianconeri won the opener 1-0 away to Frosinone, but lost Kenan Yildiz for three months to a broken metatarsal, with Weston McKennie, Khephren Thuram and transfer-listed Edon Zhegrova also out of action. Jhon Lucumi got his first start for the club , with Jonathan David used in a trequartista role. The Ducali lost at home to Cagliari and lost Hans Nicolussi Caviglia to surgery this week.

TURIN, ITALY – AUGUST 29: Luciano Spalletti, Manager of Juventus, and Carlos Cuesta, Manager of Parma, pose for a photo before the Serie A match between Juventus and Parma Calcio at Allianz Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

Douglas Luiz volleyed off target and Christian Ordonez's effort was deflected wide off Pierre Kalulu, but Francisco Conceicao was unlucky to see his daisy-cutter from outside the area clip the base of the upright on 33 minutes.

There was another opportunity for Douglas Luiz, a weak header straight at the goalkeeper from the Kalulu cross, but Lucumi almost scored on his debut when volleying over from a smart corner kick routine and dinked Jeremie Boga assist.

David also failed to keep his shot down after a poor clearance, prompting jeers from the frustrated crowd, then Kolo Muani scuffed wide after a sensational Conceicao nutmeg to get away from Emanuele Valeri.

TURIN, ITALY – AUGUST 29: Francisco Conceicao of Juventus is challenged by Emanuele Valeri of Parma during the Serie A match between Juventus and Parma Calcio at Allianz Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

There were very loud jeers from the crowd when David and Boga made way for Kerim Alajbegovic and Nico Gonzalez, and it almost had an immediate effect, because within minutes the Argentina international hit a magnificent volley from the edge of the area, denied by the even better one-handed Edoardo Corvi save.

Nico Gonzalez made an extraordinary impact, as moments later he unleashed a shot from a huge distance that cannoned off the upright, it ricocheted back into his path and the second attempt went in off Mariano Troilo.

TURIN, ITALY – AUGUST 29: Douglas Luiz of Juventus passes the ball under pressure from Christian Ordonez and Mandela Keita of Parma during the Serie A match between Juventus and Parma Calcio at Allianz Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

Parma responded immediately, as Guglielmo Vicario made a desperate one-handed save to claw the David Romero header off the line.

Kolo Muani completed a give and go with Nico Gonzalez to force another Corvi save, then nodded the resulting corner over the bar from six yards.

TURIN, ITALY – AUGUST 29: Randal Kolo Muani of Juventus runs with the ball under pressure from El Bilal Toure of Parma during the Serie A match between Juventus and Parma Calcio at Allianz Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

Parma had penalty appeals for an Alajbegovic challenge on Mandela Keita, but there was another problem for Juve when substitute Andrea Cambiaso hobbled off with a right ankle injury.

His replacement scored moments later, as Teun Koopmeiners drilled into the far bottom corner from just inside the area on a Manuel Locatelli lay-off, after Nico Gonzalez had caught Konate napping playing out from the back.

The Miami Dolphins are cutting down their roster from 91 players to 53 this weekend to comply with the league's rules before the deadline on Sunday at 6:00 p.m. ET.

While most of these moves will likely be cuts for Miami, they've decided to make a trade on Saturday, as NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that the Dolphins are sending quarterback Quinn Ewers to the Jacksonville Jaguars . It's unclear exactly which picks are involved, but ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the two teams are swapping 2028 Day-3 picks.

Miami took Ewers in the seventh round of the 2025 NFL draft following a collegiate career at Ohio State and Texas, where he earned All-Conference honors twice. In three starts with the Dolphins as a rookie, he led the team to a 1-2 record while completing 66.3% of his passes for 622 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions.

While Ewers entered this offseason as the main backup, he never really took advantage of the opportunities the team gave him. Now, he'll go back up Trevor Lawrence, and the Dolphins will have to decide who will support Malik Willis.

articles.summary: BUFFALO, N.Y. (WIVB) — The Bills began the process of trimming down to their initial 53-man roster before Sunday’s deadline by releasing 13 players, includin...
articles.body:
BUFFALO, N.Y. (WIVB) — The Bills began the process of trimming down to their initial 53-man roster before Sunday's deadline by releasing 13 players, including veteran wide receiver and kick returner Mecole Hardman.

The other players released on Saturday were: OLB Cade Denhoff, CB Jordan Dunbar, G Bruno Fina, ILB Theron Gaines, C Sincere Haynesworth, DL Zion Logue, CB D.J. Miller, S Wande Owens, WR Dante Pettis, LB Otis Reese IV, WR Quentin Skinner, TE Shane Zylstra.

Hardman joined Buffalo's practice squad last November in his seventh NFL season and was elevated to the active roster for two regular season games and the divisional playoff loss against the Denver Broncos. He was considered to be a candidate to make the 53-man roster as the primary punt returner for the Bills, but had an inconsistent performance throughout training camp and preseason.

Logue, a third-year defensive tackle, has been a member of Buffalo's practice squad the past two seasons. He has been elevated to the active roster for five games in his career.

The rest of the players released on Saturday were undrafted rookies or free agent signings who were not expected to make the 53-man roster. Some of the players could be signed back to the practice squad next week.

The Bills must cut down to 53 players by 6 p.m. Sunday. They can place two additional players on injured reserve with designations to return after four weeks of the regular season. Additionally, wide receiver Tyrell Shavers is eligible to be placed on the physical unable to perform list and could be added to the active roster later in the season.

articles.summary: The Brazilian has said ‘too many times’ that he wants to leave the club, according to his manager
articles.body:
Richarlison is one three Tottenham players who have asked to leave the club, manager Roberto de Zerbi has revealed.

Richarlison was left out of the Spurs squad for Saturday evening's 2-0 defeat by Newcastle United , having started last weekend's 3-0 loss at Brentford.

And De Zerbi said after the game that the Brazilian had requested to leave the club, naming him with defender Kevin Danso and midfielder Pape Matar Sarr as a trio of wantaway players.

"Richarlison, he said too many times that he wanted to leave," said De Zerbi. "Danso came to me two days ago and said he wanted to leave. Sarr the same, but he also suffered a small injury, but he is almost ready to train.

"I love these players and these are great guys. I have very good relationships. But if they want to leave they have to bring the economic solution to the club and they can go, and we'll find other players."

Spurs have spent around £300m on transfers this summer in a bid to dramatically turn around their fortunes on the pitch following a 17th-placed finish last season.

The club are still searching for more additions before Tuesday's deadline, although they are set to miss out on key target Cody Gakpo, the Liverpool and Netherlands winger, who is widely reported to be on the verge of an £85m transfer to Manchester City.

articles.title: Bills will replace grass field at new stadium before home opener
articles.summary: Large divots were a problem during the preseason.
articles.body:
When the Bills played their first preseason game at their new stadium two weeks ago, a "massive clump" of sod went flying, "roots, dirt, and all." One unnamed player even said, " The field is ass right now ."

So, basically, the grass is ass — and the Bills are getting out something more than a lawnmower.

Lance Lysowski of the Buffalo News reports that the entire surface will be replaced before the Week 2 Thursday night home opener against the Lions.

It will be the first of three straight home games for the Bills.

The Bills aren't conceding that the current field, which passed pregame inspection for Thursday night's preseason finale against the Steelers, is enough of a problem to require replacement.

"You can be happy with the performance and playability and still make the change," Bills chief operating officer Pete Guelli told Lysowski. "As an organization, we're committed to having the absolute best possible playing surface for the players. If it's even slightly better, we're going to make the change and err on the side of performance."

The issue was divots. The goal will be to reduce their frequency and size.

"It's not a cure-all," Bills senior director of grounds Aaron Ramella told Lysowski. "We're still going to have divots. It's a living grass field. We'll be better than where we're at now. There will be a random push or random divot. That's football. We're not playing on a rug anymore."

That's the best news. But one of the realities (and expenses) of a grass field is that it takes effort (and money) to make it high-quality. Although an overwhelming majority of players prefer grass to artificial turf, most would prefer a fake field to shoddy sod.

England's Marco Penge and New Zealand's Daniel Hillier are the joint leaders of a British Masters that is still playing catch-up after storms hit the opening couple of days at the Belfry.

Penge and Hillier are both on 11 under after completing five holes of round three before play was suspended by darkness at 19:56 BST.

Play will resume at 07:00 BST on Sunday. The weather is forecast to be largely dry in the morning with heavy rain blowing in through the afternoon and into the evening.

More than nine hours of play was lost on Thursday and Friday at the Warwickshire course.

Penge, 28, played 32 holes on Friday, carding an eagle, 10 birdies and one bogey. He was 11 under after 14 holes when play was halted by fading light and returned on Saturday morning to finish his second round on 10 under overall.

That was enough to hold the halfway lead by one over Hillier.

"It was pretty typical of me to have a roller coaster sort of round of golf. Luckily this one was on the right side of par," said Penge.

The pair then headed out in round three at around 18:30 BST and they ended the day one shot clear of Northern Ireland's Tom McKibbin, who has played six holes.

articles.title: Packers make first roster cut, officially sign veteran TE Jonnu Smith
articles.summary: The Packers released safety Tra Fluellen to make room on the roster for veteran tight end Jonnu Smith on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers made their first cut on the path to an initial 53-man roster, releasing safety Tra Fluellen to make room on the roster for the previously reported signing of veteran tight end Jonnu Smith.

Fluellen, who spent the 2026 season in the UFL, signed with the Packers on Aug. 11. He appeared in all three preseason games, playing 54 snaps on defense and seven on special teams. Fluellen is the first cut following the team's preseason finale win over the Arizona Cardinals on Friday night.

The Packers needed to make a roster move to make room for Smith, who is entering his ninth NFL season after spending last year with Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. A versatile tight end with a long history of receiving production, Smith has 345 career receptions and 30 career receiving touchdowns. He played under Matt LaFleur with the Tennessee Titans in 2018.

Speaking with the Packers Radio Network before the preseason finale on Friday night, LaFleur called Smith a "great guy" in the locker room and an "explosive" player on the field.

"I think he has a lot of versatility, moving him around. He'll bring some juice to our offense," LaFleur said.

Smith caught 38 passes for only 222 yards and two scores with the Steelers last season, but he was a Pro Bowl for the Miami Dolphins in 2024, when he caught a career-high 88 passes and scored eight touchdowns.

The Packers have to reduce their roster to 53 players by Sunday afternoon. It can be safely assumed that Smith will be one of the team's tight ends along with Tucker Kraft.

The Packers did not immediately assign a uniform number to Smith. He will likely pick one after final cuts are made.

As was the case a year ago, North Carolina began its 2026 season by scoring first against TCU. But this time, that wasn't the only highlight for the Tar Heels in their season opener.

UNC opened Year 2 of the Bill Belichick era in Dublin, Ireland, on Saturday, picking up an upset 15–10 victory over the Horned Frogs in the Aer Lingus College Football Classic. The Tar Heels' victory stood in stark contrast to a year ago, when TCU beat UNC 48–14 in Belichick's highly anticipated Chapel Hill debut.

Starting the season 1-0 is no small feat for the Tar Heels, who entered the 2026 campaign with less buzz and more baggage than a year ago. Most notably, the program placed general manager Michael Lombardi on paid administrative leave in late July as the university investigated a personnel complaint against the longtime Belichick associate. Meanwhile, UNC defensive coordinator Steve Belichick—Bill's son—has been out on medical leave since Aug. 6 and didn't coach against TCU on Saturday. In his place, Bill Belichick himself took over defensive play-calling duties, the first time he's called plays full-time since his final season with the Patriots in 2019.

Yet despite the preseason distractions, the Tar Heels looked much improved from the UNC team that amassed a disappointing 4–8 record (2–6 in the ACC) during Belichick's debut season in 2025. That's not to say the Tar Heels are now a College Football Playoff—or even ACC—contender, or that the program's unique NFL-centric approach has been validated. Still, the six-time Super Bowl champion head coach now has his first signature win at the college level.

Among the encouraging signs for the Tar Heels on Saturday was the play of quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. under new UNC offensive coordinator Bobby Petrino. The Wisconsin transfer, who carries a nearly $1.3 million NIL valuation according to The NIL Standard database, threw for 232 yards against the Horned Frogs, more than any Tar Heels quarterback amassed in a single game last season.

The UNC defense also looked vastly improved after ranking 66th nationally in points allowed per game in 2025. While some of the Horned Frogs' struggles on Saturday were self-inflicted, the Tar Heels took advantage of their opportunities, limiting TCU to 281 total yards and 1-for-5 on fourth-down conversion attempts.

But regardless of how they got there, it's already easy to sense a newfound optimism surrounding the UNC program—especially considering that the win came in the national spotlight of the first FBS game of the 2026 season. The Tar Heels entered Saturday's contest as a 9.5-point underdog at some sportsbooks, a point spread indicative of the public's expectations (or lack thereof) for the 74-year-old Belichick's second UNC season.

Of course, it's just one game and plenty can still change for a Tar Heels program that the ACC media voted to finish 15th out of 17 teams in its preseason poll . It's also worth noting that the Lombardi situation remains unresolved and it remains to be seen when Steve Belichick will return as the team's defensive coordinator. In other words, it's far too early to point to Saturday's win as evidence that UNC is now the NFL's "33rd team ," as Lombardi once dubbed it in an effort to distinguish the Tar Heels as a pro-level program.

But should Saturday's victory be a sign of things to come for UNC, the Tar Heels' success would undoubtedly become one of the biggest storylines of the college football season. That would, in turn, have significant implications for the ACC's primary media rights holder, ESPN, as well as the program's own NIL efforts.

With a game against East Tennessee State on Sept. 12 to follow UNC's upcoming bye week, a 2–0 start to the 2026 season appears to be all but a foregone conclusion in Chapel Hill. That could also set up a high-profile matchup against ACC rival Clemson on Sept. 19, as Belichick tries to make good on the buzz that accompanied his move to the college level a year ago.
